chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Mis'mam from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"When he enters [Mecca] with his offering animal during the ten [days of Dhu al-Qadri], if he has marked it and tied a cord around its neck, he should not slaughter it except on the Day of Sacrifice at Mina. And if he has not marked it nor tied a cord, he should slaughter it in Mecca when he arrives during the ten [days]." And whoever is obligated to offer a camel due to a vow but cannot find one, then upon him is seven sheep. And if he cannot find them, he should fast eighteen days, either in Mecca or when he returns to his people. Narrated.

key_terms.الْعَشْرِ: The ten days of Dhu al-Qadri at the start of Hajj
key_terms.قَلَّدَهُ: Tied a cord around its neck
key_terms.يَوْمَ النَّحْرِ: The Day of Sacrifice (10th of Dhu al-Qadri)

ai.seo_question: What are the rules for slaughtering the Hajj offering animal and the compensation if a camel is unavailable?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the procedural nuances of the Hajj *hady*, distinguishing between animals prepared with *ihsar* (marking and tying) versus those not yet prepared, thereby guiding pilgrims on the precise location and timing of slaughter. It further establishes the hierarchy of *kaffarah* (expiation) for unfulfilled vows, prioritizing animal sacrifice over fasting, a ruling consistent with Shia jurisprudence on compensatory acts. The text underscores the importance of intention and physical preparation in determining the validity of ritual obligations during the sacred days of Dhu al-Hijjah.
